tasks.title: Compact databases
tasks.what: Checkpoint, optimise and vacuum the server's database and every loop's record; a record's designs kept once (a running loop's too, a few rows at a time).

tasks.title: Condense run logs
tasks.what: A loop's log over a size keeps its recent part; the older part is gzipped beside it.

tasks.title: Bring task journals up to date
tasks.what: A loop's task journal written before the engine said what each task is (D1233) is rewritten in today's format, once, by the rules Live read it by: each task's box, pass, design and try, how each try ended, the bookkeeping as notes. The original is kept beside it (events.jsonl.orig.gz). A running loop is left until it stops.

tasks.title: Condense task journals
tasks.what: A loop's task journal (the Live tree's history) over a size keeps its recent starts whole; older ones are gzipped beside it.

tasks.title: Thin old transcripts
tasks.what: A loop's transcript (every model and agent turn: its prompt, reply and tool calls) keeps its last days whole; an older turn keeps only what usage counts -- when, who, tokens, cost, whether it failed and why. Insights reads the usage log, summed as turns happen. Running loops too: a turn is appended on its own.

tasks.title: Prune old agent folders
tasks.what: A loop's working folders of passes started more than the days ago (each agent's prompt, drafts and scratch) go -- its newest folder always stays, and the journal, the transcript, the record and the workbench. Running loops too: an old pass's folder is not written to.

tasks.title: Prune stale records
tasks.what: Record rows measured under other inputs (D853): the loop no longer counts them. Reports them; deletes them when told to.

tasks.title: Prune empty starts
tasks.what: Starts that did nothing -- stopped before any search, design, check or measurement began (D987) -- go: their row, and for a loop's latest start its log and journal. Starts already checked are left.

tasks.title: Rerun baseline
tasks.what: The loop's next start measures pass 0 again, once (D1005): otherwise a baseline on record stands while the document's baseline: section is unchanged, whatever else changed.

tasks.title: Invalidate + re-evaluate all
tasks.what: After the checks or measurement scripts change (D988): one run checks and measures every design on record again; the earlier results stay as history, no longer counted. Started on one loop only.

tasks.title: Check database integrity
tasks.what: Read-only SQLite integrity checks on the server database and stopped loops' out/*.db records. Reports problems without repairing or deleting data.

tasks.title: Validate loop documents
tasks.what: Load each stopped loop's selected problem document, including referenced parts. Reports errors without changing files or running tools or agents.

/file?path=README.md.x:
# macarray/ -- the MAC processing element's microarchitecture, on real ASAP7 numbers

The array is given: `lanes` products summed per cycle at the precision the workload IR
declares (int8 x int8 by default, from the application's `workload.yaml`). What is
searched is inside the PE:

| knob | values | what it changes |
|---|---|---|
| multiplier | `behavioral` (the `*` operator), `array` (sign-magnitude shift-and-add), `booth4` (radix-4 Booth), `wallace` (carry-save tree), plus anything a model invented | how each product is formed |
| reducer | `chain`, `tree`, `csa` | how the products (and the accumulator input) become one sum |
| pipeline | 0, 1, 2, 3 | register stages: products; plus the output; plus a cut through the reduction |

48 points (4 x 3 x 4), plus every multiplier `invent.problem.yaml` kept. The study is two
documents and the commands of `flux_macarray.steps`, one per phase (D798) -- no world:

| box | what runs |
|---|---|
| `orchestrate` | a sweep over the space; the multiplier knob also takes every file in `out/invented/` (`from: "out/invented/*.sv"`) |
| `generate` | `steps gen {artifact} {multiplier} {reducer} {pipeline}`: the PE's RTL (`rtl.py`) |
| `test` | `steps check {artifact} {pipeline}`: **Verilator** against golden vectors seeded from the workload (every lane at each corner, each lane alone at each corner, 200 random rows; D868), the latency checked against the stages the PE claims |
| `measure` | `fluxpreset rtl measure --stage synth` (the **screen**: Yosys + OpenSTA, seconds, optimistic) and `--stage place` (**OpenROAD**, the number a report may quote) |
| `select` | the objectives: at least 1000 MHz placed, then the least area; the design they choose is always placed, the rest of the finalists spread along the fmax-vs-area frontier |

```bash
cd flux
nix develop --command flux task check applications/macarray/problem.yaml
nix develop --command flux task run applications/macarray/problem.yaml --passes 1        # screen and place the space
nix develop --command flux task run applications/macarray/problem.yaml --passes 1 --screen-only
nix develop --command flux task run applications/macarray/invent.problem.yaml --passes 3 # a model invents multipliers
```

`budget.batch: 48` screens the whole space in one pass. The record and the decided PE go to
`applications/macarray/out/` (`macarray.db`, `macarray.sv`; the invention's `macarray.invent.db`);
a resumed run re-measures nothing, because measurements are keyed on the design, the stage's
command and the tool fingerprints.

## Changing the ask

Copy the folder -- its name is the copy's id, so its record and measurements do not mix with
the original's -- and edit the copy's `problem.yaml`: the clock is the stages' `--clock-ps` and
the `fmax_mhz` objective's `goal`; the lanes and the workload are the step commands'
`--lanes N` and `--workload FILE`; the space is `orchestrate.space`.

```bash
cp -r applications/macarray applications/mac16
# edit applications/mac16/problem.yaml: --lanes 16 on gen and check, --clock-ps 667 and goal: 1500
nix develop --command flux task run applications/mac16/problem.yaml --passes 1
```

## What the model does

Nothing in the PE study: a 48-point space is screened exhaustively and needs a judge, not a
proposer. `invent.problem.yaml` asks a model for a **multiplier structure the enumeration does
not contain** -- one combinational module `mult_inv` (`a`, `w` in, `p` out) -- refused before
any tool runs if it is sequential, uses SystemVerilog casts, or is the behavioral `a * w`;
then Verilator against every product, all 65,536 for int8 (`steps mult-check`, D868), its failures fed
back up to `repair_attempts` times, and the screen of the standard PE built around it (`steps
mult-screen`) as its measurement. Every multiplier that passes is kept in `out/invented/`
(renamed by its content) and joins the PE study's space on its next run.

## Layout

`problem.yaml` is the PE study, `invent.problem.yaml` the invention. `lib/src/flux_macarray/` holds
what the step commands are made of: `steps` (the commands), `config` (the space and the
shape), `rtl` (the generator), `verify` (golden vectors and the Verilator verdict), `invent`
(the multiplier's rules and golden model), `measure` and `objective` (the PE's score).

/file?path=invent.problem.yaml.x:
# A model invents a signed multiplier for the MAC PE; every one that passes its golden vectors
# is kept in out/invented/ and joins the PE study's space (problem.yaml) on its next run (D798).
#     flux task run applications/macarray/invent.problem.yaml --passes 3

statement: >-
  Design a signed 8x8-bit integer multiplier for an 8-lane multiply-accumulate processing
  element on a 7nm-class standard-cell library (ASAP7). The PE sums the products of all lanes
  every cycle; the multiplier's delay and area set the array's frequency and size. Build the
  product from partial products -- a Booth recoding (radix-4 or radix-8), a compression tree
  (3:2 or 4:2 compressors), a modified Baugh-Wooley array, a recursive split -- some structure
  with a reason to be faster or smaller than the behavioral `a * w`.
contract: |-
  ONE module named exactly `mult_inv`:
    - input  logic signed [7:0]  a
    - input  logic signed [7:0]  w
    - output logic signed [15:0] p        p == a * w as signed integers, for EVERY input
  Purely combinational: no clock, no reset, no registers. Verilog-2001 constructs only (wire,
  assign, always @(*), case, +, -, <<, &, |, ^, ~); no size casts like 8'(x), no packages, no
  functions, no generate, no $ system tasks. Not `assign p = a * w;`. Under 60 lines.
language: systemverilog

objectives:                     # measured inside the standard PE (behavioral tree, combinational)
  - {metric: fmax_mhz, direction: maximize}
  - {metric: area_um2, direction: minimize}

flow:
  test:
    multiplier: {run: "{python} -m flux_macarray.steps mult-check {artifact} --keep {home}/out/invented", timeout_s: 300}
  measure:
    screen: {command: "{python} -m flux_macarray.steps mult-screen {artifact} --clock-ps 1000",
             metrics: [fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count], needs: [yosys, openroad]}

budget:
  steps: 3
  repair_attempts: 4
  prototype: false

/file?path=problem.yaml.x:
# A MAC processing element: every multiplier, reducer and pipeline depth the generator spells,
# plus the multipliers `invent.problem.yaml` kept (D798: the study is this document and the
# commands of `flux_macarray.steps`, one per phase -- no world).
#     flux task run applications/macarray/problem.yaml --db demo-macarray.db
#     flux task run applications/macarray/invent.problem.yaml     # a model invents multipliers

statement: >-
  One MAC processing element, 8 lanes at the workload's precision (int8 x int8, accumulated):
  the smallest PE that makes 1000 MHz placed on ASAP7, chosen from every combination of
  multiplier, reducer and pipeline depth the generator can spell, plus every multiplier the
  invention problem kept.

language: systemverilog

objectives:
  - {metric: fmax_mhz, direction: maximize, goal: 1000}      # the clock it must make
  - {metric: area_um2, direction: minimize}                  # then the smallest

flow:
  orchestrate:                 # the search: every point, screened, then the finalists placed
    policy: sweep
    space:
      multiplier: {values: [behavioral, array, booth4, wallace], from: "out/invented/*.sv"}
      reducer: [tree, chain, csa]
      pipeline: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    seeds: [{multiplier: behavioral, reducer: tree, pipeline: 0}]    # the incumbent
  generate: {command: "{python} -m flux_macarray.steps gen {artifact} {multiplier} {reducer} {pipeline} --invented {home}/out/invented"}
  test:
    verify: {run: "{python} -m flux_macarray.steps check {artifact} {pipeline}", timeout_s: 300}
  measure:
    screen:
      command: "fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --stage synth --clock-ps 1000 --module mac_pe"
      metrics: [fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count]
      needs: [yosys, openroad]
    confirm:
      command: "fluxpreset rtl measure {artifact} --stage place --clock-ps 1000 --module mac_pe"
      metrics: [fmax_mhz, area_um2, power_w, cell_count]
      needs: [yosys, openroad]
      timeout_s: 1800
  select: {finalists: 4}

budget:
  prototype: false
  batch: 48                    # the whole space screened in one pass (3 reducers x 4 depths x the multipliers)
  workers: 0                   # 0 = the machine decides

/file?path=workload.yaml.x:
# Pure-einsum, fully-static-bounds example: the flagship case the affine core was designed for
# (docs/ir.md) and the one that actually round-trips through a real ZigZag evaluation
# (evaluators/zigzag/). Contrast with llama3-8b-decode-layer0.yaml, whose dynamic bounds
# (`s`/`t` as {dyn: [...]}) are exactly what ZigZag *cannot* consume — see
# evaluators/zigzag/src/flux_evaluator_zigzag/workload_translator.py's NotExpressibleError.
schema_version: "0.1.0"
id: mlp/gemm0
provenance:
  source: handwritten
  importer: flux-manual@0.1
tensors:
  - {name: I, rank: [B, C], dtype: int8}
  - {name: W, rank: [C, K], dtype: int8}
  - {name: O, rank: [B, K], dtype: int16}
ops:
  - id: mlp.gemm0
    kind: einsum
    # Dim names C/K (rather than more generic names) are load-bearing here: they must match
    # evaluators/zigzag's default target — ZigZag's bundled tpu_like accelerator + its default
    # spatial mapping, which spatially unrolls loop dims literally named K and C across its
    # 32x32 array (see zigzag/inputs/mapping/default.yaml). B is free — it stays a temporal
    # loop. Any other dim names are equally valid Flux IR but would need a different ZigZag
    # mapping to evaluate (see evaluators/zigzag/README.md's documented v0.1 gap).
    expr: "B C, C K -> B K"
    bounds: {B: 4, C: 32, K: 32}
    precision: {I: 8, W: 8, O: 16, O_final: 8}
